subject.title: fix: accept valid MCP tool schemas without strict inputSchema.type check

question: Should OpenClaw depend on the pinned MCP SDK’s private `Client.cacheToolMetadata()` method to preserve output-schema and task-support semantics after custom `tools/list` validation?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically careful, but the SDK exposes no supported public hook for injecting a differently validated page into its metadata cache; choosing a private runtime seam is a long-term dependency and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Accept the pinned private seam
options.body: Merge with the existing existence pin and behavioral parity tests, accepting that MCP SDK upgrades require direct review of this private method.

options.title: Require a public SDK boundary
options.body: Pause this branch while OpenClaw or the MCP SDK provides a supported way to cache metadata from a custom validated tool-list response.

recommendation.title: Accept the pinned private seam
recommendation.body: Merge with the existing existence pin and behavioral parity tests, accepting that MCP SDK upgrades require direct review of this private method.

likelyOwner.reason: Their maintainer-owned adjacent work covered invalid-tool quarantine and SDK metadata-cache preservation in this exact bundled-MCP catalog boundary.
